references.text: Isaiah prophesies that the Lord will remove the staff of bread from Jerusalem and Judah as a judgment.
Ezekiel describes how God will break the staff of bread in Jerusalem, and the people shall eat bread by weight with anxiety.
Ezekiel repeats the warning that God will break the staff of bread and send famine.
Ezekiel mentions again that God will break the staff of bread as a judgment over an unfaithful land.
The psalmist tells how God called forth famine and broke every staff of bread.
Isaiah describes a time when the people shall eat but not be satisfied, corresponding to the curse in Leviticus.
Hosea prophesies that they shall eat but not be satisfied, as a consequence of unfaithfulness to the Lord.
Micah prophesies that the people shall eat but not be satisfied as part of God's judgment.
Haggai describes how the people eat but are not satisfied, as a sign of God's displeasure.
During the famine in Elijah's time, the widow in Zarephath had only enough flour for one baking, illustrating scarcity of bread.
